Hi Sophie — thanks for the redline and the clear ask. Looping in Marcus (account lead) and Kim from Legal.

Short practical answer up front: we can be flexible on governing law in certain enterprise deals, but in that case we typically: (a) keep arbitration as the primary forum for disputes and (b) add an explicit interim-relief carveout that permits either party to seek provisional injunctive relief in the chosen court to preserve rights (injunctions/replevin) while arbitration proceeds. That approach preserves our ability to rely on arbitration's cost & speed benefits while giving you the immediate protection the team needs.

I attach a short draft (temp-relief-clause-proposals.txt) with three wording options: narrow emergency-only carveout; broader provisional measures carveout; and a middle ground that ties injunctive relief to IP/confidentiality/data-risk. My read: for procurement comfort, the middle ground usually lands.

Proposed next steps: 1) Marcus to confirm commercial terms are acceptable if we accept CA as governing law (we typically ask for CA or Delaware but can accept CA here), 2) Legal to agree on which carveout language to include, and 3) we do a 20-min call to close. Marcus — can you confirm the concession on law is OK (we may want to keep venue/arbitration seat as CA as well rather than forcing international forums)?

Hi all — quick legal perspective and suggested precise language (copied below). High-level: we are comfortable conceding governing law = California for this cohort of customers provided the carveout is tightly scoped so it does not swallow arbitration. If Greenline insists on very broad emergency relief (e.g., "any" provisional measures without nexus to arbitration), we will need to reserve the right to seek expedited relief in arbitration as well.

Suggested middle-ground clause (for your redline):
"Notwithstanding any agreement to arbitrate, either party may promptly apply to a court of competent jurisdiction for provisional or interim injunctive relief solely to preserve the status quo, protect Confidential Information, or prevent the unauthorized use or disclosure of intellectual property or customer data. Such application shall not be deemed a waiver of the right to arbitration or of any remedies available in arbitration. Except for such provisional relief, the parties agree that any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively by binding arbitration in the State of California under the rules of the American Arbitration Association, and judgment on the award rendered by the arbitrator(s) may be entered in any court having jurisdiction."

Rationale: that language (a) limits relief to preservation/critical data/IP, (b) makes clear seeking interim relief in court does not waive arbitration, and (c) keeps arbitration as the exclusive remedy for the underlying dispute.

Kim (Legal) — attaching temp-relief-clause-proposals.txt with marked options and a short comment line for each. If Greenline wants a broader carveout, we should agree commercial offsets (credits or shorter SLOs) — that will be a commercial negotiation.
